title: webgpu-q: Browser-native quantum chemistry and a browser-tab swarm that scales Hartree–Fock to C₆₀
description:
webgpu-q is an electronic-structure stack — Hartree–Fock (RHF/UHF), MP2, CCSD, CCSD(T), density-functional theory across the LDA/GGA/hybrid ladder, and EE/IP/EA-EOM-CCSD — that runs entirely inside a web browser with no installation, no server, and no CUDA. Numerical hot paths (electron-repulsion integrals, the auxiliary-basis density-fitting B-tensor, the Fock build) are hand-written in Rust compiled to WebAssembly with SIMD128; the methods are ported from PySCF with attribution, so the contributions are the delivery mechanism, the SIMD kernels, and the distribution layer.

A browser-tab swarm partitions the density-fitted Fock build by auxiliary index across N same-origin browser tabs coordinating over BroadcastChannel and SharedArrayBuffer; the partial Coulomb and exchange matrices sum to reproduce the single-tab build to a relative error of order 1e-15. The swarm raises the single-tab memory ceiling and scales Hartree–Fock to C₆₀ buckminsterfullerene (300 basis functions, STO-3G) on a 16 GB consumer laptop, distributing the 1.82 GB three-index tensor across four tabs at 454 MB each. Energies are validated against PySCF (bit-for-bit where the algorithm is identical; ≤ 50 µHa for HF and ≤ 0.25 mHa for CCSD(T) vs FCI otherwise).

This deposit archives the source and two manuscript drafts compiled to PDF with verified, DOI-bearing references: paper/main.pdf (the electronic-structure stack and browser-tab swarm, with validation, scaling, memory-wall, and swarm-protocol figures) and paper/main-fusion.pdf (the kernel-fusion companion characterizing the WebGPU per-dispatch ceiling). Both LaTeX sources (main.tex, main-fusion.tex), their bibliographies (refs.bib, refs-fusion.bib), and the matplotlib figure generator (paper/make-figs.py) are included. The repository carries 845+ unit tests under continuous integration plus end-to-end browser benchmarks; every reported number is traceable to a committed experiment artifact under experiments/results/.
notes: Methods ported from PySCF are Apache-2.0 (see LICENSE-PYSCF and NOTICE); original code is MIT. Generative AI was used as a coding and writing aid; all output was author-reviewed and validated against PySCF and the test suite (see the manuscript's AI-usage disclosure).
